subject: Roadmap tradeoffs: BYOK rotation & short-term retention carveouts
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@caduceus-health.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@caduceus-health.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on BYOK rotation and short-term retention carveouts

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. We have two narrow but urgent asks from our DPO and infra teams before we can move forward with a private deployment PO:

1) BYOK rotation policy: can Redwood support customer-triggered key rotation (rotate root key + rewrap without service interruption) and provide an audit trail that shows which key version encrypted which customer blobs? Our compliance team needs evidence that rotated keys were used for subsequent writes and that older keys are retired from usage after a configurable grace window.

2) Short-term retention carveouts: we need a policy to retain some categories of audit logs for only 14 days (instead of Redwood's default 90) due to data minimization rules for a subset of PII-derived traces. Can you confirm whether retention can be overridden per-log-category and whether extracts for auditor review can be scoped to those reduced windows?

I've attached a short questionnaire and a sample retention matrix for reference. We appreciate a quick triage so we can decide timing for our procurement.

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of Security, Caduceus Health

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@caduceus-health.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on BYOK rotation and short-term retention carveouts

Alice — thanks for the clear asks and the attached matrix. Looping in Laura (Compliance/Product), Marcus (Serving/Runtime), and Priyom (Retention/Orchestration) to triage.

Quick responses up front so you have visibility while we dig in:
- BYOK rotation (customer-triggered): this is currently supported with a planned seamless rewrap flow, but there are caveats around cache invalidation and active in-flight requests that we need to verify for zero-downtime guarantees.
- Per-category retention overrides: our retention engine supports per-resource policies (by index/type) but the UI/tenant-experience for per-log-category short windows is not yet exposed in the Private control plane; we can do it via API config and an exception flow.

Marcus, Priyom, Laura — can each provide the short technical note (1–2 bullets) on feasibility, risk, and an estimated ETA for a self-serve control vs. a manual exception process?

Action items for Caduceus: if you can flag which log categories must be 14 days and which can stay at 90, that will speed our recommendation.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@caduceus-health.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on BYOK rotation and short-term retention carveouts

High level notes — marking technical feasibility and risks:

- BYOK rotation (customer-triggered):
  * We support key versioning and rewrap via our KMS integration. Customer can call the "rotate" API which will create a new key version and trigger rewrap of metadata; large data rewrap happens lazily on write.
  * Risk: existing in-memory KV caches and long-lived model contexts (KV caches) may still reference older ciphertext keys for in-flight tokens. We need a short grace period where old key remains readable for decryption to avoid request failures.
  * Auditability: we record key_version_meta for every blob write and expose that in audit logs; we can include a key_version column in CSV extracts.

- Per-category retention overrides:
  * Backend: retention is applied at the object-store layer per "log_type" tag. We can enforce 14-day TTL for specific types.
  * Orchestration caveat: Private control plane currently lacks UI, but the API and infra config allow it. The operational path today is an exception ticket that we can automate in the next sprint.

ETA: low-effort config path (manual exception + API override) = 1–2 business days to enable for a new tenant. Self-serve UI + policy builder = 6–8 weeks (product + infra work).

I'll demo the audit CSV export showing key_version mapping in our next call.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@caduceus-health.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on BYOK rotation and short-term retention carveouts

Adding orchestration detail and operational controls:

- Short-term retention carveouts:
  * We can map log categories to retention policies in the retention-config service. For Private tenants we will create a policy override key scoped to a tenant + log_category.
  * For evidence exports: we can generate ad-hoc exports scoped to a time window and log types; exports are delivered as encrypted bundles to a preconfigured S3/GCS bucket.

- Exception workflow (recommended for initial rollout):
  * 1) Customer signs exception with PoA (email ok)
  * 2) SE/AE files a PR to the tenant config (automated script)
  * 3) Orchestration applies policy and we validate retention TTL on a sample set

ETA: implementing the manual exception path for a single tenant = 1 business day (testing + verification). We should also document the steps and include a short checklist for the CS handoff.

Priyom Das
Senior Product Manager, Retention & Orchestration

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@caduceus-health.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@caduceus-health.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on BYOK rotation and short-term retention carveouts

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups so we can finalize our legal/ops ask:

- For BYOK rotation: what should we expect as the grace window for decryption of older blobs to avoid request failures? Is there a recommended default (e.g., 15s, 1m, 5m, 1h) or is it workload-dependent? Can Redwood support a configurable grace window for our tenant?

- For evidence exports: we want the export to include a column that maps event -> key_version for every write and the hash of the object. Is that doable for auditor review?

- Finally, on SLA: if we apply the 14-day retention carveout will Redwood commit to not including that data in long-term analytics pipelines that might rehydrate beyond the 14 days? We need a written contract clause to that effect.

If you prefer, we can take a 30-minute call tomorrow to sign off.

—Alice

From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@caduceus-health.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, erik.morales@medsys-partners.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on BYOK rotation and short-term retention carveouts

Alice — thanks for the precise follow-ups. Short answers and next steps:

- Grace window: default recommendation is 1 minute for most interactive workloads; for high-throughput streaming customers we recommend 5 minutes while caches flush. We can make the grace window configurable per-tenant; Marcus and Priyom will add a tenant-config knob (min=15s, default=60s, max=1h).

- Evidence exports: yes — we can include key_version and object_hash columns in the audit CSV. We'll add that to the export template and provide a sample CSV in the follow-up.

- Contract language for carveouts: Legal is comfortable with an addendum that states Redwood will not copy specified short-term-retention categories into long-term analytics, with an auditing clause to ensure we honor TTLs. I'll coordinate with Legal and share draft contract language by EOD Friday.

Next steps:
- Marcus: provide a short demo/export sample (key_version mapping) and confirm where in the CSV the key_version appears.
- Priyom: stand up manual exception for Caduceus (1 business day).
- Kim: schedule a 30-minute sign-off call with Caduceus for Tue 5/18 or Wed 5/19.

If that works, I'll put the legal addendum in motion and attach the sample export once Marcus posts it.

Thanks all — Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Compliance & Privacy, Redwood Inference
